column13: Holding in one line

column2: Amitabh Bachchan v. Rajat Nagi & Ors.
column12: Can strangers use a celebrity's name, image and voice to sell goods and run lotteries without consent?
column13: Ex parte injunction granted; unauthorised commercial use of his name, image, voice and persona restrained.

column2: Digital Collectibles Pte Ltd & Ors. v. Galactus Funware Technology Pvt Ltd & Anr.
column12: Does using cricketers' names, images and stats on NFT player cards in a fantasy game breach their publicity rights?
column13: Interim injunction refused; public information and creative cards are free speech and imply no false endorsement.
column14: C.B.C. Distributing v. MLB Advanced Media (US, 2007)

column2: Krishna Kishore Singh v. Sarla A. Saraogi & Ors.
column12: Can a dead actor's father stop a film on his son's life by relying on the son's personality rights?
column13: Injunction refused; privacy and personality rights end with death and are not inherited; damages claim survives.
column14: R. Rajagopal v. State of T.N. (1994)

column2: Anil Kapoor v. Simply Life India & Ors.
column12: Does personality-rights protection reach AI deepfakes, face morphing, GIFs and voice imitation of an actor?
column13: Ex parte injunction granted expressly covering AI, deepfakes and morphing; domains and links ordered blocked.
column14: R. Rajagopal v. State of T.N. (1994)

column2: Jaikishan Kakubhai Saraf alias Jackie Shroff v. The Peppy Store & Ors.
column12: Can an actor stop merchandise, an unlicensed AI chatbot and online videos that trade on his name, voice and image?
column13: Injunction granted incl. against the AI chatbot, but a YouTube tribute video was left up as artistic expression.

column2: Dr Devi Prasad Shetty & Anr. v. Medicine Me & Ors.
column12: Can a well-known surgeon stop doctored videos using his face and voice to sell health products?
column13: Ex parte injunction granted; misuse of his persona, incl. by AI or deepfake, and the hospital's marks restrained.

column2: Rajat Sharma & Anr. v. Tamara Doc & Ors.
column12: Can a journalist stop AI-doctored videos showing him endorsing medicines?
column13: Ex parte injunction granted against misuse of his name, voice and likeness, incl. via AI and deepfakes.

column2: Sadhguru Jagadish Vasudev & Anr. v. Igor Isakov & Ors.
column12: Can a spiritual leader stop AI-morphed videos and voice deepfakes of him used in scams?
column13: 'Dynamic+' John Doe injunction granted so new mirror sites and channels can be blocked as they appear.

column2: Aishwarya Rai Bachchan v. Aishwaryaworld.com & Ors.
column12: Can an actor stop AI chatbots, AI-generated videos and fake merchandise using her persona?
column13: Ex parte injunction granted; misuse through AI, generative AI and deepfakes harms dignity as well as money.
column14: Anil Kapoor v. Simply Life India (2023)

column2: Abhishek Bachchan v. The Bollywood Tee Shop & Ors.
column12: Can an actor stop AI-made explicit images and fake images of him with others, and branded merchandise?
column13: Ex parte injunction granted; AI depictions in misleading or vulgar settings also intrude on privacy.
column14: Anil Kapoor v. Simply Life India (2023)

column2: Karan Johar v. Ashok Kumar/John Doe & Ors.
column12: Can a filmmaker remove memes, AI voice tools and merchandise that use his persona, including parody posts?
column13: Vulgar posts and AI misuse taken down; posts that were parody or lampooning were left up.
column14: D.M. Entertainment v. Baby Gift House (2010)

column2: Akkineni Nagarjuna v. www.bfxxx.org & Ors.
column12: Can an actor stop adult sites and sellers using his name and image, including through AI?
column13: Ex parte injunction granted; covers AI, deepfakes and face morphing; URLs to be removed in 72 hours.

column2: Hrithik Roshan v. Ashok Kumar/John Doe & Ors.
column12: Can an actor remove AI-morphed content and also shut down fan pages that use his image?
column13: Infringing posts removed, but whole fan pages were not taken down; only specific posts were.
column14: D.M. Entertainment v. Baby Gift House (2010)

column2: Sonakshi Sinha v. Character Technologies Inc. & Ors.
column12: Can an actor stop AI companion chatbots that impersonate her and produce obscene content?
column13: Ex parte injunction granted incl. against AI chatbot platforms; URLs to be removed within 36 hours.
column14: Anil Kapoor v. Simply Life India (2023)

column2: Allu Arjun v. Frankly Retail Pvt Ltd & Ors.
column12: Can an actor stop a paid AI voice-cloning tool, fake-call apps and merchandise using his persona?
column13: Ex parte injunction granted over his name, likeness and marks, incl. AI, voice cloning and deepfakes.

column2: Arjun Kapoor v. Artist Booking Company & Ors.
column12: Do AI-made explicit videos and fake bookings using an actor's persona escape liability as parody?
column13: Injunction granted; parody may cover a few posts, but AI explicit content must come down at once.

column2: Shashi Tharoor v. Ashok Kumar & Ors.
column12: Can a politician stop AI deepfakes and voice clones showing him making statements he never made?
column13: Injunction granted; his name, voice, speaking style and vocabulary are protected under Arts 19 and 21.

column2: Raghav Chadha v. Ashok Kumar John Doe & Ors.
column12: Can a politician get a blanket takedown of AI-generated satire and criticism of his change of party?
column13: Only 6 of 52 posts (vulgar ones) removed; political satire stays; politicians must not be thin-skinned.
column14: Kartar Singh v. State of Punjab (1956)

column2: Alakh Pandey v. John Doe(s) & Ors.
column11: O 39 R 1-2 CPC; s 79 IT Act
column12: How far can a founder use personality rights to remove online content about him?
column13: Relief limited to vulgar portrayal, monetisation and impersonation; parody, caricature and reporting protected.
column14: D.M. Entertainment v. Baby Gift House (2010)

column2: Janhvi Kapoor v. Ashok Kumar/John Doe & Ors.
column12: Can an actor get one blanket order against 6,884 URLs said to misuse her persona?
column13: Blanket order refused as over-broad; only 552 pornographic URLs removed; rest to be sorted into categories.
